name: Norman J. Colman
bio: As U.S. Commissioner of Agriculture (spelled Coleman in the paper), he appears in 1885 working to stamp out cattle disease in Missouri, questioning Texas cowmen with a view to easing the quarantine, and reading a paper at the National Cattle Growers' Association meeting in Chicago that November. In 1886 the paper reported he had sent botanist George Vasey to study the grasses of the arid West.
